title: perf(anomaly): bound the tick's outbound calls to 4 and read baselines first

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 9/10** · safe to merge The permit bound and prefetch are sound and pinned by the new model tests; only the miss-then-write path of the new raw cache key has no assertion. 1 note · tests partial −1 · risk medium Bounds the anomaly tick's warehouse and cache calls to four in flight with a `Semaphore` and reads each org's three baselines before its detector fan-out. The bound is correct and no permit path nests; only the new cache write is untested. - `withOutboundPermit` caps every tick warehouse query and baseline cache call at 4 - `readCachedBaselines` prefetches the three baselines per org before the detector fan-out - Baselines move from `getOrCompute` (hashed key) to `rawGetDetailed`/`rawPut` (raw `orgId:hour` key) - `rawGetDetailed` now annotates `cache.slots_held` ### Findings
🔵 Note · F1 · New tests never write a baseline, so the raw-key write-through is unverified tests · [`packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AnomalyDetectionService.test.ts:399-400`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/b916c802a25a229b0ae593aa8e64908204b83ec0/packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AnomalyDetectionService.test.ts#L399-L400) `warmBaselineBackend` answers every `anomaly-*base` read with `[]` (a hit) and its `put` is a no-op, so `baselineOrCompute`'s `onNone` branch — the new `rawPut` under the `orgId:hour` key that the next tick reads back — never runs in these tests, and `baselineScans` stays 0 whether or not that write works. Only the permit budget is pinned; the repopulation the first post-deploy tick depends on is not. ``` Add one case on a storing backend (`makeMemoryBackend()` for the base buckets, no `put` override) that runs `runTick` twice and asserts the first tick issues each `*Baseline` query once, while the second surfaces no `*Baseline` context at all. ```
### Production impact
Production traffic of the changed files (last 7 days) | File | Calls/day | Busiest operations | | --- | ---: | --- | | `packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AnomalyDetectionService.ts` | 8.6k | `AnomalyDetectionService.fetchErrorSpikes` 8.6k/day, 0.0% err |
Telemetry this change adds and removes (2) - ➕ span name `AnomalyDetectionService.readCachedBaselines` · `packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AnomalyDetectionService.ts:331` - ➕ attribute `maple.anomaly.baseline_hits` · `packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AnomalyDetectionService.ts:345`
What was checked - No permit is taken inside another: the `rawPut` tap runs after the compute query's permit is released (`AnomalyDetectionService.ts:324`) - Write and read use the identical `orgId:hour` key (`:335`, `:983`); `rawPut`/`rawGetDetailed` take raw keys, `getOrCompute` hashes, so the two paths cannot collide - `Semaphore.withPermit` releases on failure and interruption, so a failed org cannot starve the lane's remaining orgs

## Maple review

🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge
The write-through gap F1 is now pinned by a real storing backend, and the new budget tests would fail without the semaphore.
<sub>no findings · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable</sub>

Bounds the anomaly tick's outbound calls with a 4-permit semaphore and prefetches the three hourly baselines before the detector fan-out, so cache reads no longer queue behind warehouse fetches. The added tests pin both the budget and the baseline read-after-write, and nothing in the change is unsafe to merge.

- `withOutboundPermit` gates every warehouse query and baseline cache read/write in the tick
- `readCachedBaselines` prefetches the three 7-day baselines before the detector fan-out
- Baseline entries move from `getOrCompute` (hashed) to `rawGet`/`rawPut` (raw `orgId:hour`)
- `rawGetDetailed` now annotates `cache.slots_held`

### Fixed since the last review

- ✅ ~~F1 · New tests never write a baseline, so the raw-key write-through is unverified~~

<details><summary>What was checked</summary>

- Permits are only held around leaf calls, never nested, so the 4-permit semaphore cannot deadlock against the 6-connection pool
- `makeMemoryBackend` really stores, so the new tick-over-tick test would fail if the write used a different key
- Cache entries are plain values end to end: `getOrCompute` stored them unencoded, so the raw-key round trip keeps the same JSON shape

Only the test file changed since 8f5602f; its assertions match `claimOrg`, the real bucket names and the shared `orgId:hour` key.
<sub>no findings · tests covered · risk medium · 2/2 new units observable</sub>

Adds the tests that pin the anomaly tick's new outbound budget: one baseline round-trip across two ticks, plus a six-connection Worker model asserting at most four calls in flight and no slot wait. Safe to merge; the assertions match the code they pin.

- `ANOMALY_OUTBOUND_PERMITS` semaphore (4) bounds warehouse queries and baseline cache I/O in the tick
- `readCachedBaselines` prefetches the three baselines per org before the detector fan-out
- Baseline entries move from `getOrCompute` to `rawGetDetailed`/`rawPut` under the raw `orgId:hour` key
- `rawGetDetailed` now annotates `cache.slots_held` on its span
